title: Rationale for Newer Property Developments in Collective Sales
what_it_is: Rationale for Newer Property Developments in Collective Sales

sections.label: En bloc consent and age
sections.summary: The Land Titles (Strata) Act requires 90% consent for buildings under 10 years old and 80% for older ones; 13 of 40 en bloc sales in three years were under 30 years old.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The Land Titles (Strata) Act requires buildings less than 10 years old to obtain 90% consent from owners before allowing the collective sale to go through, compared to 80% for older developments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Of the 40 developments sold En bloc in the past three years, 13 were less than 30 years old at the point of sale.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That said, most of them were more than 20 years old at the point of sale and were small developments of less than 20 units each.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In terms of the number of housing units, around 240 units, or 6% of the approximately 4,000 units sold En bloc in the last three years, were less than 30 years old.

sections.label: URA approval and safeguards
sections.summary: Developers must submit plans to URA for approval covering planning considerations, heights, unit sizes, parking and traffic impact analysis before en bloc developments proceed if consent thresholds are reached.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Even if the consent thresholds are reached, the developer will have to submit their development plans to the Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) for approval.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: URA will go through the plans, look at planning considerations, make sure that heights and unit sizes are kept to regulations; that adequate provisions, for example, are made for parking, and we have now put in place a new provision, which is, to do a traffic impact analysis before the developer gets planning approval.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, with all these frameworks in place and safeguards, we would allow En bloc developments to go through if, indeed, the consent thresholds are reached, if the market feels that an En bloc is economically viable.
